name: Deane Mowrer
bio: Deane Mowrer was an associate editor of the Catholic Worker, one of ten pacifists jailed in July 1957 for refusing to take shelter during New York City's compulsory 'Operation Alert' civil-defense drill — an act of conscientious protest against preparations for nuclear war. She was sentenced to 30 days in the workhouse.
charges: Violating the New York State Defense Emergency Act — refusing to take shelter in a civil-defense drill

name: Richard Moses
bio: Richard Moses was a young pacifist arrested in Times Square carrying anti-war signs during New York City's July 1957 'Operation Alert' civil-defense drill, in protest against nuclear-war preparations. He was sentenced to 30 days.
charges: Violating the New York State Defense Emergency Act — refusing to take shelter / protesting the civil-defense drill

name: Jane Moses
bio: Jane Moses was a young pacifist arrested with her husband Richard in Times Square during New York City's July 1957 'Operation Alert' civil-defense drill for an anti-nuclear protest. She was sentenced to 30 days.
charges: Violating the New York State Defense Emergency Act — protesting the civil-defense drill

name: Enrique Medina Fernandez
bio: Enrique Medina Fernandez was one of five Spanish sailors who deserted a Franco naval vessel and crossed into the U.S. at Tijuana on July 4, 1957 seeking political asylum. Held by U.S. immigration authorities and ordered returned to Spain under a 1902 treaty by a Los Angeles federal court, they fought removal — backed by the ACLU — fearing imprisonment, torture, or death under Franco.
charges: U.S. immigration detention; ordered returned to Franco Spain under a 1902 treaty
convicted: Detained 1957; return ordered, then stayed pending appeal
sentence: Held in immigration detention; deportation fought

name: Gines Martinez
bio: Gines Martinez was one of five Spanish sailors who deserted Franco's navy and sought asylum in the United States in July 1957. Held by the immigration service and ordered returned to Spain by a Los Angeles federal court, he and his comrades — defended by the ACLU and the Committee to Save the Five Spanish Sailors — fought their forced return.
charges: U.S. immigration detention; ordered returned to Franco Spain
convicted: Detained 1957; return ordered, then stayed pending appeal
sentence: Held in immigration detention; deportation fought

name: Victor Rodriguez
bio: Victor Rodriguez was one of the five anti-fascist Spanish sailors who deserted a Franco warship and claimed political asylum in the United States in July 1957. The U.S. held them for return to Spain under a 1902 treaty; their case, likened to the seizure of Morton Sobell from Mexico, was fought on appeal.
charges: U.S. immigration detention; ordered returned to Franco Spain
convicted: Detained 1957; return ordered, then stayed pending appeal
sentence: Held in immigration detention; deportation fought

name: Manuel Fernandez Rodriguez
bio: Manuel Fernandez Rodriguez was one of five Spanish sailors who deserted Franco's navy and sought asylum in the United States in July 1957, then were held by U.S. immigration authorities and ordered returned to Spain. The ACLU's A. L. Wirin charged the men had been 'shanghaied.'
charges: U.S. immigration detention; ordered returned to Franco Spain
convicted: Detained 1957; return ordered, then stayed pending appeal
sentence: Held in immigration detention; deportation fought

name: Augustine Cabrera Oroza
bio: Augustine Cabrera Oroza was one of the five Spanish sailors who deserted a Franco naval vessel and sought political asylum in the United States in July 1957. Held by the immigration service and ordered returned to Spain by a Los Angeles federal court, the five fought their forced repatriation through the Court of Appeals.
charges: U.S. immigration detention; ordered returned to Franco Spain
convicted: Detained 1957; return ordered, then stayed pending appeal
sentence: Held in immigration detention; deportation fought
